summary: Re-verification of milestone M3 after commit fec2a222b reclassified every *-DESC-02 description-headroom finding to INFO in the five access/object checkers. F-29 is CLOSED AT SOURCE: milestone test M3-T2 (check_custom_permissions.py --manifest-dir artefacts --strict) now exits 0 from the build directory, printing CP-DESC-02 as INFO with 'Headroom only -- never fails the run, even under --strict.' The fix was verified rather than trusted, with two negative controls on a scratchpad copy: the assertion --strict was declared for still bites (an unresolvable $Permission.Bypass_Ghost consumer reference exits 1 under --strict, 0 plain) and the real 255-character limit still ERRORs without --strict at 271 characters. All five declared milestone tests now stand at their declared outcome; 4 of 4 executable/structural tests pass, 0 fail. Nothing else in the build changed - no artefact is newer than the first report, 41/41 references still resolve, the deploy order is unchanged, and the merged manifest was re-derived, compared identical and deliberately not rewritten. Verdict remains not-ready and now rests on ONE ground: M3-S05 is blocked. Per AGENT.md Step 1 a blocked-with-a-reason step is verifiable but its verdict is not-ready, because the decision to accept a known gap belongs to the human at G3. Absent M3-S05 this milestone would return ready-with-findings. A correction to the first run's own framing is recorded: of the three grounds it gave, only 'failing test' and 'blocked step' are Step 9 triggers - the API-version conflict was an escalated finding, not a verdict trigger. All six G3 decisions are now taken by the operator and recorded. One of this agent's recommendations is retracted: the 'third option' of setting replyToEmail to support@acme.example was wrong, and the cited skill said so six hours before the run - assignment-rules gotcha 6 names 'senderEmail (or replyToEmail)' in the loop pattern, and decisions.md D-M3S04-04 had already considered and rejected it. The auto-response artefact is correct exactly as built. One new finding: F-34, decision 3 is only half-writable because amend-step refuses 'title' on a documented step and --prose-only's allowlist excludes it. F-30, F-31, F-32, F-33 remain open; F-32 in particular is NOT closed by decision 2, because M4-S03's flow does not exist yet. Recorded with set-milestone --status rejected. No sf command, no mock_deploy.py, no org contact, no gate write, no amend-step; nothing deployed.
confidence_rationale: Step 10 rubric, LOW branch, on its first named trigger and now its only one: a step was blocked (M3-S05). The two facts that independently capped the first run below HIGH are both gone - no declared acceptance test fails any longer, and the merged manifest's version conflict is now a decided item rather than an unresolved one - but neither was the binding constraint then and neither is now. Reference resolution remains complete at 41 of 41 with zero unclassifiable. LOW measures how much of M3 the checks could see, not how well it is built: four of five steps are documented and every declared test stands at its declared outcome.

M3-T5 is type manual and is carried to the human checklist rather than executed. M3-T3's Omni-Channel clause passes vacuously because M3-S05 produced no components.

findings.detail: Closed by commit fec2a222b, which reclassified every *-DESC-02 description-headroom finding to INFO across the five access/object checkers so it never fails a run even under --strict, while leaving DESC-01 (over the documented limit) an ERROR. Re-run from the build directory: exit 0, 'Summary: 0 error(s), 0 warning(s), 1 info.' with the CP-DESC-02 line now reading 'Headroom only -- never fails the run, even under --strict.' Verified rather than trusted, because a checker that stops failing is indistinguishable from a checker that stopped checking. Two negative controls on a scratchpad copy: (1) the assertion --strict was declared for still bites — $Permission.Bypass_Ghost exits 1 under --strict and 0 plain; (2) the real limit still blocks — a 271-character description ERRORs on CP-DESC-01 without --strict. The remedy taken was this report's recommendation (c), fixing the exit policy at the checker rather than editing an accepted milestone's artefact. Recommendation (a) is now unnecessary and should NOT be done. decisions.md F-16 (M2 headroom, half open) closes by the same commit.

findings.title: The Web-to-Case channel's dependence on the bypass grant is documented but reaches no checklist line
findings.detail: artefacts/M3-S03/deploy-order.md section 6 records that both intake channels rely on Bypass_Case_Intake_Validation to pass M3-S01's rules, that the Permission Set carrying it (Case_Intake_Integration, M2-S01) must be assigned to the identity the channels save as, and that assignment is an org action outside this build - and that if the identity cannot hold it, 'every intake save fails ... a rejection the submitter never sees, because the web form still returns its retURL success page'. After the F-26/F-27 rebuild the exposure narrowed to one channel, and section 0 of the same file says so: email cases arrive with Origin stamped and Priority Medium so neither rule fires; web cases arrive with Origin Web stamped but Priority blank, because WebToCaseSettings has no priority element (three children, api_meta L112128 ff.). So at the end of M3, with M4 not built, Priority_Required_On_Agent_Save fires on every Web-to-Case submission (~60/day) unless the web save identity holds the bypass. M4-S03's before-save flow would also close it - before-save record-triggered flows run ahead of custom validation rules - but that step is pending and is itself subject to G3 decision item 2. Appears in no skipped_manual[] line in any tests/<step>/results.json.
findings.recommendation: NOT closed by decision 2. Option (2) makes M4-S03's before-save flow the mechanism, but M4-S03 is pending and unbuilt, so Web-to-Case (~60/day) still depends on the bypass grant reaching the web save identity. Checklist line 9 stands and must be ticked or explicitly accepted at G3.

findings.title: G3 decision 3 is only half-writable: M3-S04's title cannot be corrected while the step is documented
findings.detail: Decision 3 takes D-M3S04-02 option (b) — correct the step's title and the W02 manual test to Origin-only. Checked against the writer rather than assumed. W02's text is writable now: it is an acceptance_tests[].description, and amend-step --prose-only accepts notes and acceptance_tests at any status except running, with an already-approved step gate no obstacle. The title is not: 'title' is amendable only under full amend-step, which is refused unless the step's status is pending or blocked, and M3-S04 is documented; --prose-only's allowlist is notes and acceptance_tests only. Confirmed from build_plan.py amend-step --help, not only from the standard. Same shape as O-M3S02-03, where the undeclared deploy-order.md on five steps is unfixable for the same reason.
findings.recommendation: Three writes, for their owners — this agent makes no plan.json write but the one set-milestone call. (1) amend-step --prose-only on M3-S04 to re-word W02 to Origin-only, citing D-M3S04-02 option (b); that is the artefact a human ticks, so it is the one that has to be true. (2) Record in decisions.md that steps[M3-S04].title still names Account-support-tier routing, is known wrong and is unfixable in place — the treatment O-M3S02-03 gives its analogue; do not rebuild M3-S04 to fix a title. (3) Planner v6 backlog, beside api_version: 'title' belongs in --prose-only's allowlist — it decides no output, checker or edge, and this is the second decided correction blocked by a text-only field sitting behind a structural gate.

process_observations.observation: F-29 was closed at the layer that caused it. The cheap fix was to shorten one description in an accepted milestone; the fix taken was to reclassify the headroom rule across all five checkers so a future advisory cannot retroactively fail a gate on an artefact nobody is changing. That also closed M2's F-16, which had been half-open since the previous gate, without anyone re-opening M2.

The reclassification was surgical and survives both negative controls: --strict still exits 1 on the unresolvable-consumer WARN it was declared for, and the over-limit DESC-01 still ERRORs without --strict. A blunter fix - dropping --strict from the test, or making the whole checker advisory - would have produced the same green while retiring a real assertion.

This agent proposed a sender-identity option that the cited skill had already ruled out in one sentence, and that decisions.md D-M3S04-04 had already considered and rejected - both readable at the time of the run. The failure was not a missing source; it was reasoning past sources that had been opened. Worth noting because the run's confidence was LOW for an unrelated reason and would not have flagged it.

Two of the six G3 decisions cannot be fully executed against plan.json as it stands: decision 3's title half (F-34) and, from the previous run, the undeclared deploy-order.md outputs on five steps (O-M3S02-03). Both are text, both are blocked by a status gate written for substantive amendments. A build accumulating known-wrong prose it is not permitted to fix is how a plan stops being readable as a record.

Decision 2 reads like it closes F-32 and does not. Option (2) names M4-S03's before-save flow as the mechanism that stamps Priority ahead of the validation rule, but M4-S03 is pending and unbuilt, so the ~60/day Web-to-Case exposure is live between G3 and M4. A decision about a future step is not a control today, and the gate checklist has to keep carrying it.

Unchanged from the first run and still worth a human's eye: REQ-022's push half resolves against M2-S04's Queue:Tier_1_General, so traceability.md shows no coverage gap while the capability the requirement names is blocked in M3-S05.
